stages.title: UPSC RELEVANCE AND ANSWER-WORTHINESS AUDIT
stages.terms: UPSC Relevance and Answer-Worthiness Audit: No verified Mains PYQ in the routed owner makes this a separately owned Mains theme, so Mains practice below is answer-building support, not an inflated claim of official frequency.
stages.mechanism: They are not a separately named Mains syllabus unit; they are an Ancient History/culture-context answer resource.
stages.consequence: The verified 2021 Prelims site-feature question proves direct objective relevance.
stages.trap: They are not a separately named Mains syllabus unit; they are an Ancient History/culture-context answer resource.
stages.answer: Neolithic and Chalcolithic cultures are directly relevant to Prelims GS-I under History of India: chronology, site-culture-region matching, technology, crops/animals and distinctions are repeatedly testable formats.

stages.title: PART I - ROADMAP, SYLLABUS BOUNDARY AND EVIDENCE DISCIPLINE — [CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: PART I - Roadmap, Syllabus Boundary and Evidence Discipline — [CORE MAINS]: Direct official ownership is strongest in Prelims GS-I; Mains use is analytical through technology, ecology, archaeology, social change and source criticism.
stages.mechanism: FACT: Topic 05 explains the many regional transitions from foraging toward cultivation, herding and village life, followed by rural Chalcolithic cultures using copper and stone.
stages.consequence: METHOD: Static foundations come first from the authored Topic 05 files, then local OCR books.
stages.trap: Qdrant was optional, unnecessary and not used.
stages.answer: FACT: Topic 05 explains the many regional transitions from foraging toward cultivation, herding and village life, followed by rural Chalcolithic cultures using copper and stone.

stages.title: MEANING AND CHRONOLOGY - NEOLITHIC, NEOLITHIC-CHALCOLITHIC AND CHALCOLITHIC — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Meaning and Chronology - Neolithic, Neolithic-Chalcolithic and Chalcolithic — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]: METHOD: Always specify whether a date is calibrated, uncalibrated, a range, or a textbook approximation.
stages.mechanism: Chalcolithic denotes the use of copper alongside stone, not an exclusive copper technology.
stages.consequence: INFERENCE: Labels are useful for comparison but must be applied after examining local sequences.
stages.trap: Chalcolithic denotes the use of copper alongside stone, not an exclusive copper technology.
stages.answer: FACT: Neolithic conventionally combines food production with ground, pecked and polished stone tools; many sites also show pottery and more sedentary settlement.

stages.title: TRANSITION FROM FORAGING TO FOOD PRODUCTION - MOSAIC, NOT LADDER — [CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: INFERENCE: Transition is best understood as a changing portfolio of subsistence strategies.
stages.mechanism: Hunting, gathering, fishing, herding and cultivation frequently co-existed, and some mobile communities produced food while some settled communities remained strongly dependent on wild resources.
stages.consequence: INFERENCE: Food production changed risk management, labour scheduling, storage and human-environment relations, but did not make every community sedentary or prosperous.
stages.trap: INFERENCE: Food production changed risk management, labour scheduling, storage and human-environment relations, but did not make every community sedentary or prosperous.
stages.answer: FACT: Upinder Singh rejects a simple unilinear sequence.

stages.title: WHY DOMESTICATION? COMPETING EXPLANATIONS AND A MULTI-CAUSAL VERDICT — [CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Why Domestication? Competing Explanations and a Multi-Causal Verdict — [CORE MAINS]: No single theory explains every region.
stages.mechanism: METHOD: Avoid climate determinism by specifying the intermediate mechanism.
stages.consequence: FACT: Upinder Singh treats the impulses behind domestication as regionally variable and difficult to isolate.
stages.trap: METHOD: Avoid climate determinism by specifying the intermediate mechanism.
stages.answer: FACT: Archaeologists have proposed environmental stress, nuclear-zone knowledge, demographic pressure, positive feedback from productive domesticates and Holocene environmental amelioration.

stages.title: DOMESTICATION OF PLANTS - DIRECT EVIDENCE, INDIRECT EVIDENCE AND RICE CAUTION — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Domestication of Plants - Direct Evidence, Indirect Evidence and Rice Caution — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]: Plant presence is not identical to cultivation.
stages.mechanism: Archaeologists compare grain morphology, rachis behaviour, phytoliths, impressions, carbonized remains, weeds, processing equipment and field indicators.
stages.consequence: FACT: Mehrgarh yielded barley, wheat and later cotton; Lahuradewa, Koldihwa and related sites anchor rice debates.
stages.trap: Plant presence is not identical to cultivation.
stages.answer: FACT: Plant domestication involves sustained human selection and reproduction outside a purely natural cycle.

stages.title: DOMESTICATION OF ANIMALS - HERD STRUCTURE, MORPHOLOGY AND HUMAN CONTROL — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: FACT: Animal domestication is inferred from long-term morphological change, demographic profiles, geographic displacement, pathologies, residues and settlement context.
stages.mechanism: FACT: Mehrgarh shows declining wild gazelle and rising cattle, sheep and goat proportions through time.
stages.consequence: FACT: Mehrgarh shows declining wild gazelle and rising cattle, sheep and goat proportions through time.
stages.trap: METHOD: One small bone cannot establish domestication; assemblage pattern and secure identification are essential.
stages.answer: FACT: Animal domestication is inferred from long-term morphological change, demographic profiles, geographic displacement, pathologies, residues and settlement context.

stages.title: POLISHED STONE, MICROLITHS, BONE TOOLS AND THE PERSISTENCE OF OLDER TECHNOLOGIES — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Polished Stone, Microliths, Bone Tools and the Persistence of Older Technologies — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]: Bone and antler industries were especially prominent at Burzahom and Chirand.
stages.mechanism: Stone remained economically important throughout the Chalcolithic.
stages.consequence: FACT: Technology layers overlap; polished stone does not erase microliths, and copper does not erase stone.
stages.trap: FACT: Technology layers overlap; polished stone does not erase microliths, and copper does not erase stone.
stages.answer: FACT: Neolithic toolkits included ground, pecked and polished celts, axes, adzes, chisels, querns and ring stones, but microlithic blades often continued.

stages.title: POTTERY, COOKING, STORAGE AND CERAMIC CHRONOLOGY — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Pottery, Cooking, Storage and Ceramic Chronology — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]: Aceramic Neolithic is a valid category.
stages.mechanism: METHOD: Ceramic seriation must be anchored by stratigraphy and absolute dates.
stages.consequence: FACT: Mehrgarh Period I was largely aceramic; pottery increased later.
stages.trap: FACT: Cord-impressed and black-and-red wares appear in several regions but not as one uniform culture.
stages.answer: FACT: Pottery supported cooking, serving and storage, but food production can precede pottery.

stages.title: SETTLEMENT, HOUSES, STORAGE AND THE NEW TIME HORIZON — [CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Settlement, Houses, Storage and the New Time Horizon — [CORE MAINS]: It also created new risks from crop failure, pests, disease and stored-surplus loss.
stages.mechanism: FACT: Public works require coordination but do not by themselves prove a state.
stages.consequence: FACT: Storage shifts subsistence from daily acquisition toward annual scheduling and reserve protection.
stages.trap: FACT: Public works require coordination but do not by themselves prove a state.
stages.answer: FACT: Early food production often increased sedentariness, investment in houses and storage, and collective management of space.

stages.title: SUBSISTENCE, LABOUR, HEALTH AND DEMOGRAPHIC CONSEQUENCES — [CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Health evidence is sample-dependent.
stages.mechanism: INFERENCE: Labour division by age and sex likely changed, but exact roles cannot be mechanically reconstructed from ethnography.
stages.consequence: FACT: Skeletal and dental evidence at Mehrgarh and Inamgaon permits diet and health reconstruction.
stages.trap: FACT: Upinder Singh cautions against imagining farming as an easy life.
stages.answer: FACT: Farming could raise aggregate food availability and support population growth, but early farmers often faced narrower diets, infectious disease, hard labour and vulnerability to drought, pests and storage loss.

stages.title: CRAFTS, SPECIALIZATION AND EXCHANGE NETWORKS — [CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Stone, shell, semi-precious beads, copper, gold and pottery reveal local specialization and long-distance exchange.
stages.mechanism: Stone, shell, semi-precious beads, copper, gold and pottery reveal local specialization and long-distance exchange.
stages.consequence: FACT: Mehrgarh graves include materials from distant source zones.
stages.trap: FACT: Early villages were not isolated subsistence units.
stages.answer: FACT: Early villages were not isolated subsistence units.

stages.title: SOCIAL DIFFERENTIATION, HOUSEHOLD ORGANIZATION AND SETTLEMENT HIERARCHY — [CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: METHOD: Use the phrase 'suggests ranked differentiation' rather than claiming kingship unless evidence is stronger.
stages.mechanism: INFERENCE: Rank could emerge through control of storage, exchange, water, ritual or livestock.
stages.consequence: FACT: Inamgaon has interpreted craft quarters, central elite structures and a settlement hierarchy.
stages.trap: FACT: Differences in house size, settlement position, diet, burial treatment, stored wealth and craft location suggest emerging ranks at some sites, but inequality varied greatly and should not be read as a fully developed class state.
stages.answer: FACT: Differences in house size, settlement position, diet, burial treatment, stored wealth and craft location suggest emerging ranks at some sites, but inequality varied greatly and should not be read as a fully developed class state.

stages.title: RITUAL, BURIALS, FIGURINES AND THE PROBLEM OF MEANING — [SUPPORTING]
stages.terms: Ritual is inferred from patterned, non-utilitarian context.
stages.mechanism: The neutral description must precede religious identification.
stages.consequence: FACT: Mehrgarh burials included red ochre and varied grave goods.
stages.trap: Answer-use: FACT: Burials, ochre, animal interments, fire installations and figurines reveal patterned practices, but their meanings remain contested.
stages.answer: FACT: Burials, ochre, animal interments, fire installations and figurines reveal patterned practices, but their meanings remain contested.

stages.title: REGIONAL MAP IN TEXT - THE INDIAN NEOLITHIC MOSAIC — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Regional Map in Text - The Indian Neolithic Mosaic — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]: North-west is not the only early agricultural zone.
stages.mechanism: INFERENCE: Similar tools may reflect convergent adaptation, interaction or shared learning; the mechanism must be tested.

stages.title: NORTH-WEST NEOLITHIC - MEHRGARH AS A LONG SEQUENCE — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: North-West Neolithic - Mehrgarh as a Long Sequence — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]: Its long sequence records mud-brick construction, storage, microliths, early cultivation and herding, craft growth, burial change and long-distance exchange.

stages.terms: FACT: Burzahom Period I is known for round or oval pits, storage pits and ground-level hearths.

stages.answer: FACT: Kashmir Neolithic sites occupy karewa landscapes.

stages.title: VINDHYAN FRINGES AND MIDDLE GANGA - KOLDIHWA, MAHAGARA AND LAHURADEWA — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Vindhyan Fringes and Middle Ganga - Koldihwa, Mahagara and Lahuradewa — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]: Rice debate is about context, taxonomy, dating and scale.

stages.title: REGIONAL NEOLITHIC COMPARISON - WHAT VARIED AND WHAT CONVERGED — [CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Regional Neolithic Comparison - What Varied and What Converged — [CORE MAINS]: INFERENCE: Shared outcomes do not require a single origin.

stages.terms: Chalcolithic is not a uniform period.

stages.terms: Copper and Stone Technology - Ore, Smelting, Alloying and Scarcity — [SUPPORTING]: Object presence is weaker than production debris for local metallurgy.

stages.terms: Ahar-Banas Culture - River Valleys, Copper, Farming and Settlement Diversity — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]: White-painted black-and-red ware, copper use, mixed farming-herding and varied settlement sizes are major markers.

stages.answer: A seed, animal bone, tool or storage feature is evidence only in context.

stages.title: CORE LAB 3: REGION-SITE-MARKER TRIADS — [CORE PRELIMS]
stages.terms: Core Lab 3: Region-Site-Marker Triads — [CORE PRELIMS]: Do not add every excavated site unless it changes the option or argument.
stages.mechanism: A technological label names an archaeological pattern; it does not by itself name a people or a destiny.

stages.answer: Use compact triads: Mehrgarh--north-west--early farming; Burzahom--Kashmir--pit dwellings/bone tools; Chirand--Bihar--long Neolithic-Chalcolithic sequence; south India--cattle/polished axes/ash mounds; Ahar-Gilund--Banas valley--Chalcolithic; Malwa--Navdatoli/Eran/Nagda; Jorwe--Maharashtra.

stages.title: CORE LAB 5: CHALCOLITHIC IS RURAL AND REGIONAL, NOT FAILED HARAPPA — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Chalcolithic means copper plus stone; it does not mean iron, automatic urbanism or a failed version of Harappa.
